citation.title: GANTL: Towards Practical and Real-Time Topology Optimization with Conditional GANs and Transfer Learning
citation.authors: Mohammad Mahdi Behzadi; Horea T. Ilieș

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The authors present GANTL as enabling real-time design-space exploration by reusing a low-resolution GAN for high-resolution target models, with fewer fine-tuning cases.
claim.key_phrase: supports real-time generative design space explorations
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML runtime ratio is reported. The 1.85 s per iteration figure in the introduction is a background value for a separate SIMP solver, not a paired GANTL timing.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion reports 11,000 low-resolution source cases and 1,500 high-resolution target cases; tables compare pixel accuracy/compliance to SIMP for selected examples.

baseline.implementation: Freely available MATLAB 88-line SIMP code cited for ground-truth generation
baseline.hardware_classical: not stated; Introduction cites 1.85 s/iteration for a 300 × 100 MMB problem without hardware
baseline.problem_size: 40 × 80 source and up to 200 × 400 test domains
baseline.classical_time: 1.85 s per iteration is cited for a separate SIMP solver in the Introduction; no runtime for this paper's paired tests
baseline.ml_time: not stated; described qualitatively as real-time
baseline.data_generation_cost: 11,000 low-resolution and 1,500 high-resolution training cases; time/cost not reported here (Conclusion)
baseline.quality_metric: binary accuracy, MSE, compliance error, standard deviation and topological connectivity; Tables 2–5
baseline.quality_gap: Tabled errors are for displayed examples; authors report lower confidence on thin members and additional-force tests (Sections 4.1–4.2)

R1.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.2 compare predictions with SIMP using compliance and image metrics, but report selected examples and do not establish a matched quality or equal-compute comparison for the real-time claim.

R2.evidence: The Introduction cites a MATLAB SIMP iteration time, but the paper gives no paired hardware or timing protocol for the GANTL comparison.

R3.evidence: The Conclusion gives training case counts but no training or data-generation time, amortization, or explicit per-query-only scope.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.2 report compliance errors against SIMP for predictions, but do not report FE verification/constraint status and failure rates across the test set.

reporting.n_test_cases: Multiple test scenarios; one reported scenario contains 250 cases with five and ten applied forces (Section 4.2)

notes: The article refers readers to a prior paper for data-generation computational costs but does not report them in this paper.
